Company description: CVX (Generated via gemini-3.5-flash-lite)

Chevron Corporation, traded under the ticker symbol CVX, is a leading American multinational energy corporation and one of the world's largest integrated petroleum companies. Headquartered in San Ramon, California, the company engages in every aspect of the oil and gas industry, including hydrocarbon exploration and production, refining, marketing and transportation, petrochemical manufacturing, and power generation. Chevron's origins trace back to the 1879 formation of the Pacific Coast Oil Company, which later became part of the Standard Oil trust as Standard Oil of California. Following the antitrust dissolution of Standard Oil in 1911, the entity operated as Standard Oil of California and later Chevron Corporation, a name adopted following its 1984 merger with Gulf Oil, which was then the largest corporate merger in history. The company further expanded its global footprint through the 2001 acquisition of Texaco and the 2005 purchase of Unocal Corporation. Today, operating in over 180 countries, Chevron is actively managing its traditional fossil fuel operations while concurrently investing in lower-carbon technologies, such as renewable fuels, hydrogen, and carbon capture, utilization, and storage, to support the global energy transition.
